subject.title: CLI startup preflight can corrupt the live state DB while a gateway is running — health-check commands caused "database disk image is malformed" (2026.6.6, macOS); vanilla SQLite control does NOT reproduce

question: Should the shared state DB policy be RPC-first/no-maintenance CLI access, a stricter single-writer gateway lease, or both?
rationale: Source confirms mutable CLI-side DB open paths, but the durable fix changes ownership between gateway RPC observability, doctor migrations, plugin-state probes, and operator recovery behavior.

options.title: RPC-first plus no-maintenance CLI
options.body: Status, health, and stability should ask the running gateway first, and fallback file opens while the gateway is active should be read-only with no journal or checkpoint pragmas.

options.title: Single-writer gateway lease
options.body: The gateway should own the state DB write/maintenance lease, and non-gateway processes should fail closed or route through gateway APIs for writes and maintenance.

options.title: Forensic harness first
options.body: Pause implementation until the reporter's corrupt DB bundle and a native runtime harness confirm the precise OpenClaw helper/runtime interaction.

recommendation.title: RPC-first plus no-maintenance CLI
recommendation.body: Status, health, and stability should ask the running gateway first, and fallback file opens while the gateway is active should be read-only with no journal or checkpoint pragmas.

likelyOwner.reason: The choice cuts across the DB-first runtime-state architecture introduced in PR #78595 and current gateway/CLI ownership boundaries.
